runtime: Python 3.13/3.14 on supported Windows 10/11 Beta targets

arithmetic.implementation: Python integers plus decimal.Decimal only at validated input/output boundaries; persisted policy thresholds use integer seconds and integer millionths-of-percentage; source suspension is normalized to reduced rational seconds
forbidden: binary float for SLA duration/percentage decisions
premature display rounding before inclusive threshold comparison

timezone.rule: cohort month/report period/SLA ordinary calendar interpretation are fixed to America/Guayaquil; LLD-05 Objective timezone is ignored by this domain

xlsx_report_stack.writer: openpyxl write-only workbook mode behind ReportArtifactWriter interface
xlsx_report_stack.why: openpyxl is already admitted by LLD-04 and will be pinned once by LLD-12/release dependency lock; using one governed XLSX library avoids a second OOXML dependency
rules: artifact generation reads only persisted report-attempt snapshot rows, never live mutable domain tables
formulas are not used for authoritative results; represented values are written as already-calculated snapshot facts
temporary output uses same-volume atomic replace/finalization strategy where filesystem permits
artifact is reopened/validated after close and SHA-256/size are captured before completed-report publication

concurrency: Live SLA calculations are read projections. Catalog/classification/policy writes use short UnitOfWork transactions. Report snapshot materialization uses a stable read snapshot plus bounded staging writes; XLSX generation and verification occur outside writer transactions.
cache_policy: Beta 1.0 may persist rebuildable projection caches only when exact input fingerprints and invalidation hooks are present. Queries must remain correct by recomputation if caches are absent or stale.
dependency_gate: The pinned openpyxl version must pass both LLD-04 read-security fixtures and LLD-06 report-generation/golden fixtures on Python 3.13 and 3.14 before release acceptance.
